description: Given an algorithm stated as (numLogicalQubits, tCount) and a physical error rate (or hardwareId), derive the full surface-code + magic-state-distillation footprint from the general laws of the Litinski lattice-surgery cost model (no per-scenario constants): distillation factory choice, tile layout, required code distance, total physical qubits, and wall-clock time. Results are reported under TWO published logical-error fits (conservative + optimistic) because they disagree by 13-268x (d=7 to d=25) - always state both. Returns an explicit `infeasible` block when no cataloged factory or code distance can satisfy the error budget. Computes numbers only: comparing against classical alternatives and concluding "should this run on a quantum computer" stays with you, the calling agent (state the caveats when you do).

cycleTimeSeconds.description: Surface-code cycle time in seconds. Default 1 µs (Litinski convention; Google 2024 measured 1.1 µs on superconducting hardware). Trapped-ion/neutral-atom cycles are orders of magnitude slower.

dataBlock.description: Data-block layout (Litinski §2): compact = fewest qubits, fast = shortest time per T gate.

hardwareId.description: Alias for qubitErrorRate: resolves to the 2-qubit error rate of the given SOTA hardware entry from list_current_quantum_computers. Use this, not a generic qubitErrorRate such as 0.001, whenever the question names a platform without stating its own error rate (superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom). Supply exactly one of qubitErrorRate or hardwareId.

numLogicalQubits.description: Number of logical data qubits the algorithm needs.

qubitErrorRate.description: Physical 2-qubit error rate p in (0, 0.1]. Supply exactly one of qubitErrorRate or hardwareId.

tCount.description: Total number of T gates (magic states consumed). Convention: state Toffoli-counted algorithms in T gates before calling (1 Toffoli ≈ 4–7 T depending on decomposition).

targetSuccessProbability.description: Target end-to-end success probability. The failure budget (1 − target) is split evenly between T-state error and logical (memory/surgery) error, matching Litinski §4.

name: compute_fault_tolerant_resources

infeasible.description: Non-null when the scenario is infeasible as modeled: no cataloged factory meets the T-error budget (factory and layout are then null) or no distance up to the cap meets it under either fit (per-fit distance, qubits and wall clock are then null).

distance.description: Required surface-code distance (odd); null when no cataloged distance suffices.
Required surface-code distance (odd); null when no cataloged distance suffices.

results.description: Both fits bracket the model uncertainty; report both.

title: Compute Fault-Tolerant Resources
